title: Microsoft Graph
subtitle: Microsoft Graph is how the employee reads mail, posts in meeting chat and answers calls, with tokens minted per employee and validated before use.

stats.label: tools on the digital-employee server through which a model acts as the employee

lede: Helix puts a governed digital employee into Teams calls and meetings, and Microsoft Graph is the surface it acts through. The first problem was calling: no single Microsoft principal can both answer a call as the employee and own the media session. I composed two Graph Communications clients. The employee's identity answers inbound calls under its own name, and a transport-only client owns the native media platform that carries the audio. That composition is the core of A self-hosted colleague in a Teams call. The second problem was acting in meetings with attribution any model could rely on. I built a Rust MCP server for those meeting actions.
quote: I can turn Microsoft Graph into a governed action surface for an AI colleague, where every call, message and screen share is attributed to one identity and grounded in what Graph reports.
evidence: Microsoft Graph and Entra integration: two composed Graph Communications clients, so a digital employee answers Teams calls under its own identity while a transport-only client owns the media.
Identity for AI agents in Microsoft Entra: a Rust MCP server of 24 meeting tools where every call names the acting employee and the server mints that employee's token by certificate assertion.

Fail-closed agent tool design: a room-state projector over Graph participant data, joins counted only once the roster shows the employee, and a typed refusal where Graph offers no way to raise a hand.
author: Corey James
